{{Short description|Swedish physicist}}
{{expand Swedish|topic=bio}}
'''Sven Kullander''' (9 March 1936 – 28 January 2014) was a Swedish physicist.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.e-catworld.com/2014/01/swedish-physicist-sven-kullander-dies-at-78/ |title=Swedish Physicist Sven Kullander Dies at 78 &#124; |publisher=E-catworld.com |date=2014-01-31 |accessdate=2014-02-09}}</ref> He was professor of High Energy Physics at [[Uppsala University]]. Kullander received his doctorate from Uppsala University in 1971.<ref>{{cite book|last=Kullander|first=Sven|title=High-energy hadron-nucleus scattering and associated instrumentation problems.|series=Abstracts of Uppsala dissertations from the Faculty of Science, 0345-0058; 188|year=1971|location=Uppsala|url=https://libris.kb.se/bib/21116}}</ref> He took part in experiments on measurements of [[Nuclear shell model|nuclear shell]] structure from [[meson]] [[scattering]] carried out in [[Particle accelerator|accelerators]], on the structure of [[Helium]] nuclei, and on [[quark|quark structure of matter]] by meson production. He also contributed to the development of accelerators.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nobelprize.org/nobel_prizes/physics/articles/kullander/|title=Accelerators and Nobel Laureates|publisher=Nobel Media AG|accessdate=4 May 2012}}</ref>

Since 1990, Kullander had been a member of the [[Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences]] and since 2004, chairman of its Energy Committee.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://katalog.uu.se/empinfo?id=XX524_1&q=Sven+Kullander|title=Sven Kullander|publisher=Uppsala University|url-status=dead|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20140202224040/http://katalog.uu.se/empinfo?id=XX524_1&q=Sven+Kullander|archivedate=2014-02-02}}</ref>
